newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index ends 1.41 pct up in pre-budget trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index ends 1.41 pct up in pre-budget trade.

text.p: Fresh speculative buying at the start of the weekly account pushed Bombay shares to a firmer close, but off the day's early highs on Friday in the run-up to this evening's budget, traders said.
General market expectations, however ruled near low levels over likely radical reforms that the government might announce, they said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, due to present the 1997/98 budget at 5.00 pm (1130 GMT), will have to initiate a number of steps to take the economy out of a slowdown while sustaining stock market hopes by announcing certain expected measures.
"People are cautiously optimistic. I think, the market view is equally divided," said Gul Teckchandani, chief investment officer at Sun Foreign & Colonial Asset Management.

The budget which is seen as a litmus test for Chidambaram who has to cope with the political compusions of a fractious 15-party centre-left coalition is widely expected to contain no radical budgetary measures to cut expenditure, traders said.
"Clearly, we are looking for policy statements on whether the government means that reforms will be carried forward," Teckchandani said.

Market hopes include the dilution of a new minimum tax on firms, allowing companies to buy back their shares and the elimination of double taxation on company dividends, dealers said. The Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange will hold special post-budget trading from 1800-2000 local (1230-1430 GMT).
Shares of Sterlite rose 8.50 rupees or 3.5 percent, to 254.0 rupees, after the firm on Friday announced a 2.5 percent rise in its first half net profit ending December 1996.
ACC rose 82.0 rupees to 1,495.0 and Reliance 5.50 to 272.0.
